privacy: Progress is held only in this page session; no learner identity or answers are stored or transmitted.
title: Operating Cylinder Study
description: Follow the revised GTSIO-520-H cylinder through a four-stroke teaching cycle, using the same 61-component model as Explore.

lessons.title: Follow one four-stroke cycle
lessons.objective: Use the shared 720-degree crank angle to sequence the four ideal teaching strokes and relate mechanism motion to valve/cue observations.

steps.title: Piston direction at 90°
steps.prompt: Start with the mechanism. At 90 degrees, predict whether the piston is travelling away from or toward the cylinder head, then reveal the pose.
steps.note: Use Section view if you need to see the piston, rod and crank relationship.

steps.title: Rod angle at 270°
steps.prompt: At 270 degrees, inspect the changed rod angle and piston direction. What has rotated continuously while the piston reverses direction?
steps.note: The crankshaft provides the rotary-to-reciprocating relationship.

steps.title: Cycle cues: intake
steps.prompt: Turn on the illustrative cycle cues and go to 90 degrees. Predict the lesson-profile valve/stream state before looking inside.
steps.note: Cues are schematic and idealised; they do not measure pressure, temperature or real timing.

steps.title: Cycle cues: compression
steps.prompt: At 270 degrees, identify the compression region. The piston is now rising with both valves closed - compare its direction and the cue colour with the earlier intake observation.
steps.note: The four stroke labels divide a teaching 720-degree cycle (0-180 intake, 180-360 compression, 360-540 power, 540-720 exhaust); they are not manufacturer valve-event timing.

steps.title: Cycle cues: power
steps.prompt: At 450 degrees, identify the power region. The piston is descending again, as it did during intake, but the valves are closed and the cue shows combustion driving it. What has changed between the two poses?
steps.note: 450 degrees falls in the 360-540 power stroke of the teaching profile; the cue is schematic and does not measure pressure, temperature or real timing.

steps.title: Exhaust and cycle end
steps.prompt: At 630 degrees, inspect the exhaust region. Complete the cycle at 720 degrees and observe that the shared model returns to its starting state.
steps.note: A four-stroke cycle requires two crankshaft revolutions.

lessons.title: Explore how the cylinder parts fit
lessons.objective: Use staged exploded poses to identify part interfaces and distinguish a structural overview from a maintenance removal sequence.

steps.title: Assembled interfaces
steps.prompt: Rotate the cylinder and locate the rocker covers, spark plugs and piston/rod interface.
steps.note: Structural overview only. Presentation offsets do not define a maintenance sequence; permanent joints remain together.

steps.title: Valve-train relationships
steps.prompt: Trace tappet to pushrod to rocker to valve. Which parts retain the valve springs? Rotate the paused exploded pose to compare the two valve trains.
steps.note: Structural overview only. Presentation offsets do not define a maintenance sequence; permanent joints remain together.

steps.title: Permanent cylinder joints
steps.prompt: Identify the head/barrel unit and pressed guides/seats. Why are these kept together in this structural overview?
steps.note: Structural overview only. Presentation offsets do not define a maintenance sequence; permanent joints remain together.

steps.title: Piston and rod connections
steps.prompt: Locate the piston rings, floating pin, rod cap and bearing halves. Explain which interfaces guide sliding motion and which permit rotation.
steps.note: Structural overview only. Presentation offsets do not define a maintenance sequence; permanent joints remain together.

checks.question: How many crankshaft degrees make one four-stroke cycle?
checks.hint: Count the intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes, then relate them to crankshaft revolutions.
checks.rationale: Intake, compression, power and exhaust together span two crankshaft revolutions.

checks.question: Which component converts the connecting-rod force into rotary output in this study?
checks.hint: Look at the part that continues to turn while the piston travels up and down.
checks.rationale: The crankshaft receives the rod force and turns it into rotary output.

checks.question: At which positions does the piston reverse direction during its travel?
checks.hint: Use the terms top dead centre and bottom dead centre from the mechanism view.
answers: At the top and bottom of its stroke
checks.rationale: The piston reverses at its top and bottom dead-centre positions while the crankshaft continues to rotate.

checks.question: What do the coloured charge/flow cues establish?
checks.hint: Read the cue panel's What this shows note before deciding whether it makes a measured engineering claim.
answers: A schematic teaching explanation of the cycle
checks.rationale: They are illustrative, valve-gated teaching cues rather than measured fluid or timing data.

checks.question: Which observation is supported by the current operation profile?
checks.hint: Separate a checked geometric position from a physical quantity that would need its own validated model.
answers: The checked piston, rod and crank positions at a selected angle
The exact combustion temperature in the cylinder
checks.rationale: The profile checks the mechanism positions. Quantitative temperature and flow-rate claims would need a separate validated model and source.

checks.question: Put these valve-train parts in the order the motion passes through them, from the cam to the valve.
checks.hint: The motion starts where the cam pushes and ends where the valve opens.
checks.rationale: The cam lifts the tappet, the tappet moves the pushrod, the pushrod tips the rocker arm, and the rocker arm presses the valve open.

checks.question: Which parts hold a valve spring on the valve stem?
checks.hint: Look at the top end of the valve stem, above the springs.
answers: The spring retainer, locked to the stem by split keepers
The rocker shaft and the rocker cover
The valve guide and the valve seat
checks.rationale: The retainer passes the spring force to the valve, and the split keepers engage a groove in the stem to lock the retainer in place.

checks.question: Match each connection to what it allows.
checks.hint: Ask whether the parts slide, swing or turn against each other.

pairs.left: Piston rings in the cylinder bore
pairs.right: Slide along the cylinder wall while sealing gas and oil
Lets the rod swing against the piston
Let the rod turn on the crankpin

checks.rationale: The rings seal a sliding joint, the pin lets the rod change angle as the crank turns, and the bearing halves give the rod a lubricated surface to turn on at the crankpin.

checks.question: The exploded poses pull the cylinder apart so you can see it. What do they tell you about the order a technician removes parts?
checks.hint: Read the note under each step.
answers: Nothing: the offsets are for viewing and do not give a maintenance sequence
Parts move away in the order a technician removes them
The part that moves furthest is always removed first
checks.rationale: This is a structural overview. Permanent joints stay together and the spacing is only for viewing. The removal sequence comes from the manufacturer’s manual.
